question.text: In an open-ended Cat III AIF scheme, investors are permitted to:

answer.text: Redeem only at the end of a fixed maturity period (typically 5-7 years)
Subscribe and redeem units at periodic intervals (monthly/quarterly/semi-annual) at prevailing NAV, subject to cut-off and notice-period rules
Withdraw capital on demand with same-day settlement
Redeem only if SEBI grants specific permission for each redemption

explanation.text: The Logic: Open-ended Cat III schemes offer ongoing subscription and redemption at the prevailing NAV, at periodic intervals specified in the PPM — commonly monthly, quarterly or semi-annually — subject to cut-off time and notice-period provisions. The Trap: Option A describes close-ended. Option C (same-day settlement) is impractical — NAV-based subscription/redemption typically settles T+3 to T+5. Option D is fabricated; SEBI does not approve each redemption. Cross-Exam Context: Mutual funds (XXIV / XV) are daily-NAV open-ended; Cat III open-ended is similar but with notice period and higher ticket size. Manager's Pro-Tip: In your PPM, set subscription and redemption on the same calendar so you can net flows and minimise prime-broker cash drag — a mismatch (monthly sub, quarterly redemption) causes operational headaches.
